analysis: Examined the four changed files. (1) StartCommand+ClusterMember.swift: adds an `answersUpdateDrain` parameter (default false) passed into ProviderLoopConfig.clusterMemberAnswersUpdateDrain; only runClusterMember (line 95-96) sets it true. This is a local config flag. The coordinator-side drain handling and the ProviderLoop semantics are outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm that a coordinator-initiated drain message is authenticated, nor that it is limited to the paired coordinator connection. Next pass should check ProviderLoop's handling of the drain message against T-053/TB-002. (2) UpdateCommand.swift (lines 107-108, 117-118, 179-234): when no LaunchAgent is loaded but the cluster service is running, `darkbloom update` writes a ClusterPairUpdate.Request file into the cluster service directory (the owner's ~/.darkbloom/cluster-setup) and polls a progress file. The artifact download and hash verification remain in SelfUpdater and are unchanged. The request is only a restart trigger; it carries a timestamp and id, no code path or version selection. Same-UID local processes could already write that directory and fully control the owner's account, so no new boundary is crossed (same-UID adversaries are pre-existing in TB-003). The writeRequest/readProgress implementations (file permissions, symlink handling, parsing bounds) and the supervisor's request consumption are not supplied, so these remain unverified contracts. The progress is read and trusted only for display and exit status. (3) main.swift is comment-only. It notes that `--version` on stdout is compared exactly by the cluster supervisor (ClusterCandidateRecovery.startCheckFailure); MacOSUpgradeNotice.emit() writes to stdout before parsing, so if it ever emitted on stdout it would break that comparison. That is an availability/robustness concern only, not a security regression. (4) OnboardingChecks.swift adds test expectations for U.oneBuild only; no production effect. No concrete regressions were identified. Residual questions: the supervisor's validation of the update request and restart (ClusterPairUpdateCycle, ClusterServiceAgent), the drain-answering path, and whether restarting into a candidate build preserves existing candidate-recovery and quarantine checks (T-043).
